summary: Unauthenticated remote code/input execution service bound to 0.0.0.0:7000
details: w-screenctl starts a Hapi HTTP server bound to 0.0.0.0:7000 with no authentication and exposes endpoints that pass network-supplied strings directly to code- and input-execution sinks on the host. The /chrome/evaluate handler forwards the request body's `script` field into Playwright's page.evaluate, executing arbitrary JavaScript inside a browser context on the operator's machine. The /keyboard/type, /mouse/* and /screenshot handlers dispatch to execFileAsync('xdotool',...) and w-mousekey, injecting synthetic keystrokes, mouse events, and screen captures at the OS level. Because the listener binds to all interfaces rather than 127.0.0.1 and no token, HMAC, or origin check is performed, any party with network reachability to port 7000 can execute code in the operator's browser session and drive the operator's desktop input. The service fires only when the operator explicitly starts the tool (e.g. via the shipped g.mjs or a systemd unit), not on `npm install` or `require()`; however, once started it provides a persistent, unauthenticated remote control channel over the host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
